overview: A broad trough brings several rounds of snow to the West from Thursday through Saturday, with the heaviest totals in northern Utah and the Sierra early in the week. Colder air follows, and the Weather Prediction Center expects another active stretch in the West around Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A slow-moving trough brings snow in pieces from Thursday morning through Saturday morning. Southwest flow favors south-facing slopes early on. Colder air late Friday could drop snow levels to valley floors and shift the best snow toward northwest-facing terrain. Snowbasin leads with 48" total, with 27" on Friday. A winter weather advisory runs Thursday through Saturday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong storm brings heavy mountain snow through Friday morning, with gusty south to southeast winds that may cut visibility near whiteout. Snow levels fall to about 3,500 feet early Friday. Kirkwood leads with 41" total, 32" of it on Thursday. A brief lull follows, then a weaker system arrives this weekend.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A deep Pacific trough brings heavy snow and strong ridge winds through Friday morning. The heaviest snow falls Thursday afternoon through evening. Mammoth leads with 29" total, 24" on Thursday. Expect dry gaps Friday afternoon into Saturday morning, then another system arriving Saturday afternoon.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A cold front and upper trough cross the region from Thursday night into Friday, bringing snow to all elevations by Friday. Upslope flow favors the Sun Valley area and the Bighorns. Grand Targhee leads with 28" total, 12" on Friday. Light snow continues through the weekend, and the next system returns around Thanksgiving.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Thursday stays dry, then a system brings snow to the Continental Divide from Thursday night through Saturday. Southwest winds gust to 50 mph, and the San Juans get the most snow. Wolf Creek leads with 19" total, with the heaviest totals on Monday. Taos sees a smaller chance of snow early next week.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A trough crosses Friday and Saturday, with snow falling mainly on the western mountain faces. Snow levels drop to around 6,000 to 7,000 feet, and ice is possible on higher passes. Telluride leads with 12" total, with the heaviest snow arriving Monday. Steamboat and Crested Butte see lighter, scattered snow showers.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says the West stays unsettled into the following week, with a second trough bringing heavy snow to the Sierra around next Tuesday, Nov 24.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
